title: Consistent Road Geometry During Interrupted Map Updates
grain: One base/oracle OSM element or one ordered node/way edit or sequence marker
dataset: Geofabrik OpenStreetMap Monaco extracts and regional daily replication diffs
question: Can an interrupted map update publish mutually consistent node positions and road geometry?
design: Start at snapshot sequence 4897, replay sequences 4898–4926, and compare geometry at every version with a full rebuild. Track backward node-to-way dependencies and publish versioned geometry through an atomic SQLite transaction. Independently verify the terminal state against the 1 October publisher extract. Exercise replay, skipped sequence, interrupted commit and reopening.
boundary: This is a reproducible experiment on a single regional OSM extract and a local SQLite store. Work counts measure recomputation. System latency and production availability require separate measurement.
redistribution: Contains derived OpenStreetMap data © OpenStreetMap contributors under ODbL 1.0; extracts from Geofabrik.

fields.op: Put, delete or sequence commit marker
fields.road: Highway tag is present for a way
